description: How the platform selects the approach for each season (cycle), target and product from the historical and validation evidence (scripts/method_selection.py, docs/50). Fixed before further validation seasons are scored. A selection is the approach the evidence supports; the published forecast changes only by an explicit decision.

probabilities.label: Published tercile probabilities
probabilities.score: RPS of the tercile probabilities (lower is better)

amounts.label: Rainfall amounts (and ranges)
amounts.score: CRPS of the rainfall-amount forecast in mm (lower is better)

historical: A method is a candidate for a target and product only if its benchmark confirms it better than the published reference: outer leave-one-year-out over the training years (1993-2016), Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every method and target of its family, and not worse over the test years (2017 onward).

validation.rule: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py for bias correction; dist_shadow.py for the EMOS amount model). A candidate becomes 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the reference and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer it stays a 'candidate'; with enough and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'. A candidate with no validation record yet needs a shadow forecast before it can be recommended.

choice: Among candidates, a recommended one first; then the candidate with the largest training-period improvement over the reference. One change at a time: candidates from different families (e.g. an amount correction and a probability calibration) were each tested against the published approach, not together, so the selection changes one stage only; the others are listed as alternatives.

statuses.keep: Keep the published approach: no method is confirmed better on the historical evidence.
statuses.candidate: Confirmed better on the historical evidence; independent validation seasons are still being collected.
statuses.recommended: Confirmed better on the historical evidence and not worse over the independent validation seasons.
statuses.not_supported: Confirmed better on the historical evidence but worse over the independent validation seasons.
